items.correct: No — antibiotics kill bacteria, not viruses.
items.misconception: Yes, antibiotics cure colds and flu.
items.why: Viruses aren't affected by antibiotics, which is why they don't treat viral illnesses like colds.

items.correct: Weakened or inactive pathogens (or their antigens) to trigger immunity.
items.misconception: The full, active disease that makes you ill.
items.why: Vaccines expose the immune system to antigens so memory cells form, without causing the disease.

items.correct: No — only pathogens cause disease; many microbes are harmless or useful.
items.misconception: Yes, every microbe makes you ill.
items.why: Many bacteria and fungi are beneficial (e.g. gut bacteria, yeast); only pathogens cause disease.

items.q: Why do you usually not catch the same disease twice?
items.correct: Memory cells give a faster, stronger response next time (immunity).
items.random_wrong: The pathogen disappears from the world.
items.why: After infection or vaccination, memory lymphocytes recognise the pathogen and respond rapidly.

specSource: Cambridge IGCSE Biology (0610) syllabus; Diseases & Immunity
